Sequence step: raise the 0x104fd0 handshake flag and return; the screen loader (0x7e302) and the round code poll it

Sequence step re-entry stub: sets the resume PC to the child-wait body 0x7e9dc and returns (the wait itself runs in the scheduler)
Sequence step: spawn 0x7ea72 as a child, then wait until the parent flag byte ($11,parent) is set by it (0x7e9fa) before finishing at 0x7ea0a; calls 0x4c6 actor_spawn

Overlay actor: frame $9ed84 at x=0x120, priority 0x3e8, y=0x1d8 (or 0xba when ($14,a6) is negative, the -2 instance spawned by 0x7e856); allocates palette 0x102 and drifts y by ($14,a6) every frame, drawing through actor_draw; calls 0xb9a22 palette_slot_alloc
Undraws the overlay actor: passes its position to 0xd3fc (sprite-window clear) and returns; calls 0xd3fc sprite_window_clear
Sequence step: spawn 0x7ec9a as a child and hand control to 0x7ea8c (waits for it there); calls 0x4c6 actor_spawn

Sequence step: clear the word streams at $7f0f4, then push the pointer list at $7f1c0 through the queue stream 0xb9bde one long at a time (($16,a6) walks the list, -1 ends), 0x32 frames per entry; then spawns 0x7edf6 and waits 4 frames (resume 0x7ead2); calls 0xb9cb6 vram_stream_words
Timer body of 0x7ea8c: every 4 frames pops the next long from the $7f1c0 list and streams it (0xb9bde); -1 ends the step; calls 0xb9bde vram_stream_longs

Sequence step: bump the free-running counter 0x100003; every 8th tick pick the next 18-byte record of table $7f878 into ($40..$4a,a6), spawn a frame actor 0x7ebb6 from its tail words, init the animation record $7f4c6 and hold for 10 frames (0x7eb9a); calls 0x4c6 actor_spawn
Timer body of 0x7eb1a: waits 10 frames (0x68618 returns carry when the animation is done), signals the parent flag ($11) and despawns; calls 0x68618 anim_stream_step
Sequence step: allocate a palette slot (bank 0x1d), show frame $9faec at priority 0x5a, resume at 0x7ebd4; calls 0xb9a22 palette_slot_alloc

Sequence step: despawns when the parent flag byte ($44,parent) is set; otherwise places the actor on the line from the parent position through its own record endpoints (linear interpolation over the record at ($40,a6)) and draws it (0xf08); calls 0xf08 actor_draw

Sequence step: walks the 4-word records at ($40,a6) as a polyline, generating the fade/slide between waypoints through 0x57622 and advancing the cursor when the target is reached (carry set = next segment, 0xd0 = done); calls 0x57622 screen_fade_slide

Sequence step: reset the map window (0xd0f6 with 0x28/0x33/0xb4), stream the words at $7f1fa and the long list at $7f128, raise the 0x104fd0 handshake flag and continue at 0x7ecd0; calls 0xd0f6 sprite_map_blit_wrap

Sequence step: clear the handshake flag, blit the two bank maps of 0x7ee9a, spawn the frame actor $7f48e plus three palette actors 0x7ee7e (frames $9faa2/$9fab6/$9fad2, palette banks 0x246/0x247/0x241 - the podium characters), stream $7f1c0 again and wait 10 frames before the next group (0x7ed74 -> 0x7eb1a); calls 0x7ee9a blit_two_bank_maps

Sequence step: waits for the parent flag, then unless the BIOS byte 0x10fd83 is set prints 0x11ff through the print engine (0x804de), spawns the 0x7eedc fix-text actor and holds 0xb4 frames; calls 0x804de print_text

Sequence step: blit three 0x11 x 0x18-word strips from the $7f1e2 / $7f1ee pointer lists into VRAM (0xd326), shifting each strip down by 8 px when the BIOS byte 0x10fd83 is set; calls 0xd326 vram_window_blit
Sequence step: allocate the palette bank at ($20,a6), show a frame at priority 0x5f and fall through to actor_draw (0x7ee94); calls 0xb9a22 palette_slot_alloc
One-instruction thunk: jump to actor_draw (0xf08); the label in the Ghidra inventory is Ghidra's, the code is a plain tail call; calls 0xf08 actor_draw
Blits two bank map windows through 0xd2ce: 0x2474a8 as a 0x14 x 0x0b window at (0,0) and 0x247818 as a 0x14 x 0x05 window at y=0x150; calls 0xd2ce sprite_map_clear_blit
Sequence step: print the fix-layer string at $7f922 into VRAM 0x7117 through the text engine 0xd828 (d0 = 0x300 attributes); calls 0xd828 fix_text_engine

Sequence step: remember the string at $7f922, base VRAM address 0x7117 and a 0x14-frame counter; the tick body 0x7eef6 writes one character per step into the fix layer (VRAMADDR/VRAMRW at 0x3c0000), 0x20 words apart, until the -2 terminator; calls 0x54a actor_despawn
Timer body of 0x7eedc: every 0x14 frames fetch the next byte of the $7f922 string and write it as an attribute word through 0x3c0000 (VRAMADDR then VRAMRW); -2 ends the step

Sequence step: allocate palette bank 0x9f and play a scripted rise: the ($14,a6)&4 bit selects one of the two word streams at $7efc6; the actor rises 1 px per frame to y=0x1d0 while the stream supplies the priority, x offset and frame for each y step; calls 0xb9a22 palette_slot_alloc

Sequence step: animate zoom ($3a/$3b) from 0x40 upward by 5 per frame; on overflow snap both to 0xff, signal the parent flag and switch to the orbit body 0x7f01e, which moves the actor along a 0xbf-radius arc and alternates two frames from $7f200; calls 0xb9a22 palette_slot_alloc

Shared actor prologue: installs the animation stream at ($46,a6) and resets the animation counters (0x68600); entered from actor spawns where the caller has just stored the stream pointer at +0x46; calls 0x68600 anim_stream_init

Intro frame-actor body (continuation of intro_actor_script_move): holds each frame for ($40,a6) ticks while moving the actor by ($42,a6)/($44,a6) per tick; falls through from the handler head at 0x7f072; calls 0x54a actor_despawn
Second intro frame-actor head: installs ($46,a6) as the animation stream and falls into the wait body at 0x7f0b6; entered by the step stubs 0x7e822/0x7e82c at 0x7f0aa; calls 0x68600 anim_stream_init
Waits for the installed animation to finish (0x68618), then bumps the parent flag ($11) and despawns; the one-shot form of the frame actor; calls 0x68618 anim_stream_step

staff roll driver (not a per-player course introduction), spawned by results_sequence_actor 0x74946: waits 0x28 frames, then for step 0x10ecb4 reads the 6-byte record at 0x7ff4c (duration + step actor; 9 records, $ffff at 0x7ff82 marks the last), spawns the step actor, the staff-text script player 0x7fb60 and the palette fade actor 0x7fd7e (semantic-review-p1-7e726)

Advances the intro: spawns a fade actor for the step (palette 0x1f), waits 0x5a frames, then bumps the step byte 0x10ecb4 and re-enters the driver at 0x7f95a (a negative step duration ends the intro instead); calls 0x4c6 actor_spawn
Intro tail: sets the palette dirty flags for the fade-out actor, waits 0x2d frames and hands control back to the parent (the screen actor); calls 0x4c6 actor_spawn

Resets the intro state before the round starts: clears the step byte 0x10ecb4 and the handshake flag, marks the three fade flags 0x104fca/b/c as 0x1f and sets the game state 0x10ebbe to 0x0a before jumping to the course loader 0x7b50c; calls 0x7b50c course_load_dispatch

Per-step sprite script player: pushes the step palette list at 0x80014 (ids until -1) through 0xb9a22/0xb9dc6, picks the sprite script for the step from table 0x7ffee (course 0 in the BIOS-flag case uses 0x8004a), optionally spawns the banner actor 0x7fca6 when the record word is negative, and then walks the script: {u16 x, u16 y, u8 palette index, u8 op} records where op 0 = end, 0x20 = skip, 0xff = end of script and any other op is a frame index -0x41 into table 0x80210; calls 0xb9a22 palette_slot_alloc

staff-roll banner, spawned by staff_roll_text_actor 0x7fb60 at 0x7fbc0 only for step 8 (the $ffff word 0x80012): frame $a38a0, palette 0x106, y = S+$40 + $14c while P+$43 is clear, then after $3c frames rises 1 px every other frame to y=0x178, sets P+$11 = 1 and stays drawing forever (0xb9dd6 clears the slot's fade-exempt bit; it never frees the slot or finishes) (semantic-review-p1-7fca6)

Palette cross-fade actor: steps the three fade flags 0x104fca/b/c from their current value toward the target ($40,a6) by ($41,a6) per frame (direction from the sign), signals the parent ($11) and despawns when the target is reached; flags 0x104fc8 dirty for the uploader; calls 0x54a actor_despawn

odd-step staff-roll actor: sprite allocator reset (0x7b4fe, not a course unload), pose backdrop 0x7b5a2 (palette streams plus the map 0x7ba8a[course_index]), spawns pose_spawner 0x7b7fe with +$11 = P+$13 (palette-list index into 0x7bdb6) and +$13 = 0x8029c[...] - $41 (pose record index, 'G'..'L') (semantic-review-p1-7fca6)

even-step staff-roll actor: resets the sprite allocator (0xd0f6, start $28, split/end $c8; not a map window) and shows course image ((step>>1) + course) mod 4: a palette stream from 0x7ff92 ({slot, palette id} pairs via 0xb9bde) and two 20x16 sprite maps from P2 ROM via 0x7ff3c (semantic-review-p1-7fca6)

body of the even-step image: runs the 0x7ff92 palette stream through 0xb9bde (not a layer stream) and blits the two 20x16 sprite maps selected from 0x7ffce / 0x7ffde through 0x7ff3c; resumes at 0x7fec4 (semantic-review-p1-7fca6)
Course-intro actor for step 8: same layer blit as 0x7fe60 but with the fixed stream table 0x7ff84 and bank window 0x23de08 (no step arithmetic); calls 0xd0f6 sprite_map_blit_wrap
Erases the two 20x16-word map windows of the intro layer (0xd3fc) once the parent flag ($42,parent) is set, then parks at 0x7ff3a; calls 0xd3fc sprite_window_clear
Blits a 20 x 16-word map window (a0 = bank source) at the VRAM origin through the sprite-map blitter 0xd2ce; d0..d4 = 0x14/0x10/0/0/0; calls 0xd2ce sprite_map_clear_blit
Clears the pending-flush word 0x1000d2 (cancels a queued 0x0f request)
Initialises the sound-command queue state: head and tail 0x10ecd6/0x10ecd8 = 0, reply bytes 0x10ecda/db = 0, suppress flag 0x10ecdc = 0, last-char 0x10ecde = 4

Pushes byte d0 into the 32-byte command ring at 0x10ecb6 (head 0x10ecd8, masked to 0x1f); control bytes (< 0x20) are dropped when identical to the previous one; a full ring sets the last-char byte to 0xff instead

encodes a 16-bit sound code (selector high byte + request low byte): low byte < $20 ignored; high bytes $01/$02/$03 (M1 stop-all+park / stop song / restart) dropped; the demo-sound drop (MVS flag 0x10fd82 set, backup byte 0xd00046 nonzero, BIOS_USER_MODE 1 = title/demo, not developer mode) applies to high byte $00 and $10..$1f (semantic-review-p1-7fca6)

queues $0c (the M1 direct sub-command 0x210f that sets the deferred song-stop flag 0xf816; not a carriage return) and then encodes d0 through sound_cmd_send_code; nothing is printed (semantic-review-p1-7fca6)

Returns the audio latch reply: -1 when none is new, otherwise the last reply byte (0x10ecda) with bit 7 cleared and shifted right by one ((b + 0x80) >> 1); the raw byte is remembered in 0x10ecdb so each reply is reported once

Per-vblank queue drain (called from the vblank work 0xd430): if the pending word 0x1000d2 is set, clear it and write 0x0f to the audio command latch 0x320000; otherwise read the latch into 0x10ecda and send one queued byte (tail 0x10ecd6, masked 0x1f) to 0x320000
Cart vector 0x134 handler: sets the pending word 0x1000d2 so the next vblank writes the 0x0f request byte to the audio latch
One-instruction stub: push byte 0x06 into the command queue; calls 0x802de sound_cmd_putc
One-instruction stub: push byte 0x05 into the command queue; calls 0x802de sound_cmd_putc
not an entry: lies inside the dead block at 0x80460 (file 00080480.s), which queues $07, d0 + $20 (saturated), $08, then max(d1, $20) (semantic-review-p1-7fca6)
queues command $0a (M1 slot 0x2185, subcmd_fade_out; alternate entry 0x8049c queues $0b) and then d0 + $20, saturating at $ff on carry (not clamped at $20) (semantic-review-p1-7fca6)

public sound entry: encodes d0 through sound_cmd_send_code unless, in title/demo mode (0x10fdaf == 1), the DEMO SOUND soft DIP 0x10fd91 is nonzero (WITHOUT); no developer gate, no print (semantic-review-p1-7fca6)

builds 20 overlay sprite objects (header+6 sprites x header+7 tiles) from one of three panels selected by the mode word 0x10d4c0 (4 -> 0x8ac30, 5 -> 0x8ac4a, else 0x8b12c); $2f00 is the SCB1 attribute word (palette $2f, from the 0x809ae/b4/ba streams), SCB3 gets 0 / $40 (sticky); clears 0x10ecf4 and falls into overlay_list_arm (semantic-review-p1-7fca6)

Task install stub plus the overlay refresh routine it installs: the stub hands 0x80aaa (labelled overlay_refresh inside the block) to the scheduler (jmp $d510); spawned as an actor from the shot code (`lea $80aa0,a1; jsr $4c6` at 0x2f0a and 0x314a); calls 0xd510 task_install

inserts one overlay item into the list at 0x10ece8: walks while the node's y is greater than the actor y ($32,a6), so the list is in descending y ending at the y = 0 sentinel; links the new node at 0x10ece4 (semantic-review-p1-7fca6)

Copies the per-golfer byte of table 0x80bf8 (2,4,0,3,3,1) into byte +0x23 (not +3) of both player records (0x107004 P1, 0x10702a P2); ids >= 6 are skipped; +0x23 extends the power meter top (0x72286) and picks the meter bar frame (0x72a3e)

(min,max) limits of the low byte of shot_curve per golfer id from 0x80bfe: (0,8)/(1,7)/(2,6)/(1,7)/(0,8)/(0,8); stored at +$42/+$43 by 0x56284 and enforced by curve_select_state 0x562d2 (B/C) (semantic-review-p1-7fca6)

sends a sound code for the swing (not a print): 0x109e when player record +3 >= 2, else 0x109f, and 0x1022 when bag_get_club reports club type >= 10; the wood/putter reading is invented; calls 0x80f56 (semantic-review-p1-7fca6)
A single rts immediately before bag_get_club; recovered as the fall-through target of the instruction flow at 0x80f4e (the tail of the preceding source)

sets up the 32-row tournament leaderboard 0x10eda2: rows 0..30 get the course's 31 computer-golfer name pointers (list 0x83352[course]) in random order (random_range(0,30), redrawn while 0x83cc2 finds the name), +7 = $20/$30 by name-index parity; P1 -> row 31 ('PLAYER 1' 0x838f2, +7 |= $0b), P2 -> the row above (row 31 without P1; 'PLAYER 2' 0x838fb, +7 |= $0d); +6 = tee-off wave 0, -1 .. -6 per 5 rows; game_mode 0 turns row 30 into a computer row; then six 0x83ba2 calls (none in game_mode 2)

exchange sort of the 32 leaderboard rows by the signed +4 score, lowest first: row i vs every later row j, swapping when j is lower, or equal while row i is not human (+7 bit 3); a human row leads its tie, tied computer rows are reordered
writes the standing into +5 of all 32 sorted rows: competition ranking by position (ties share: 1,2,2,4)

plays one hole for the leaderboard (returns at once in game_mode 2): ranks first (0x83b72, before this hole's scores), then for each row with +6 < 18: +6 += 1 and, once +6 >= 1 (teed off), scores the hole into +4: human rows (+7 bit 3) via 0x83c24 (strokes - par), computer rows += table[(rng&7)+(rng&7)+difficulty 0x102eb8] from 0x83c50 (bytes -2..+3); re-sorts at the end

human-row branch of leaderboard_ai_advance (bne.w at 0x83bda, not called): row +4 += record +2 (strokes taken) - par of the current hole (0x5897a returns the par, not a score); row +7 bit 1 set (the P1 row) selects P1's record 0x107006, else P2's 0x10702c; rejoins at 0x83c18

computer row's per-hole score-delta table: par of hole +6 on the course (0x58988) selects the 4-long pointer table 0x83c92 (par 3), 0x83ca2 (par 4) or 0x83cb2 (par 5), +7 bits 4-5 (class 0..3) the long; each long -> a 22-byte signed strokes-to-par table 0x83904 + $16*k (-2..+3), indexed 0..21
searches the 32 leaderboard rows for the name pointer d1 (long at +0): found -> d1 = 0 and a3 = the row; absent -> d1 unchanged (nonzero); clobbers d7
resets all 32 rows: +0 = 1 (no name), +4 score, +5 rank, +7 flags = 0; +6 untouched

turns a human player's row into a computer row (adds nothing): finds the first row whose +7 has the player's bit (d0 = 0 -> bit 1 P1, else bit 2 P2), sets +7 = $30, +4 = $28 (+40 to par), +0 = the first unused course name (0x83d38); trap #15 when no row has the bit; only caller 0x6d55e in game_mode 1
returns in d1 the first name pointer of the course list 0x83352[course] not yet in the leaderboard (loops while 0x83cc2 finds it); no bound: with all 31 placed it reads past the list

standing (1..32) of a player in the sorted leaderboard: walks from the top keeping the 1-based position of the first row of the current score (ties share, as 0x83b72), stops at the first human row (+7 bit 3) with the player's bit (d0 = 0 -> bit 1, else bit 2); trap #15 when none
Clears a VRAM block through the fix-layer stream 0xd8c8 (d1 = d2 = 2); calls 0xd8c8 vram_word_stream

Returns carry set when a memory card is detected: REG_STATUS_B 0x380000 bits 4/5 are the card detect lines, low = inserted (andi.b #$30 + beq to the carry-set exit; hardware register map, docs/lanes/unibios.md; the supporting reads 0x0f with a card and 0x7f without, from a local explore_level@nocard run, are uncommitted)
Memory-card page 1: prints the three text blocks (0x84520/0x8453e/0x84546) through 0x83dc6 and arms the 0x384-frame timer before the action body at 0x83e28; calls 0x83dc6 card_clear_block
Memory-card page body: waits the timer, plays the card animations and handle the result of the save/load (see the inline notes); ends by signalling the parent screen actor; calls 0x4c6 actor_spawn
Single rts closing the card page body before the data-reset routine

Memory-card helper called at the top of the card screen (0x854a8): counts how many of the two coin consume bytes 0x10fdb6/7 are set, and when exactly one is set tries to read the card (0x843fa) - on failure, or when START is not held, it clears the whole 0x80-byte card record at 0x10eea2 and returns with carry set (meaning "use the empty record"); calls 0x843fa card_read
Waits 0x3c frames, signals the parent ($11 = 1) and despawns (the timer tail of the card page action); calls 0x54a actor_despawn

Memory-card save entry (called from the card screen): bails out when START is held, else clears the system latch registers 0x3a0005/0x3a0017/0x3a0019 and 0x380011, then runs the card command 4 (0x844f8) and the write (0x8444a); carry set reports failure; calls 0x844f8 card_cmd4

BIOS memory-card read: command 2 at 0x10fdc4, size 0x200, buffer pointer 0x10eea2 with length 0x80, then BIOS 0xc00468; carry set when the BIOS result byte 0x10fdc6 is 0 (no card / no data); calls 0xc00468 bios_card_command

BIOS memory-card write: command 3, fills the 0x80-byte record at 0x10eea2 with the 20-byte header 0x83d9e (or 0x83db2 when the BIOS byte 0x10fd83 is set), runs BIOS 0xc00468, prints the "MEMORY CARD" box (0xd7ec at VRAM 0x7000) and then BIOS 0xc0046e (write) with the VBlank flag 0x10fdc2 cleared around it; calls 0xc00468 bios_card_command

BIOS memory-card delete (command 4), FCB $200 = NGH 200, SUB 0; START/SIZE unused; calls bios_card_command $c00468. Delete semantics decoded in neo-po/neo-epo/sp-s2/UniBIOS 4.0 and observed before card writes (semantic-settle-card-demo).
Switches the input sampler to the real ports (source -1) and sets the auto-repeat word 0x10ef3a to 0x1002 (delay 0x10, period 2); calls 0x8500e input_source_select
Sets the auto-repeat word 0x10ef3a from d0 (high byte = initial delay, low byte = repeat period, in vblanks)

Selects the input source: d0 < 5 plays back demo stream d0 (table 0x84fc8 of 5 long stream pointers, 0x10ef3c = 1, cursors cleared), any other value uses the real ports (0x10ef3c = 0); the ROM byte 0x85138 (always 0 in this build) additionally requests a 0x200-byte fill of the record buffer

Per-frame input sampler (called from the round code 0x60198): for the real-port mode reads 0x10fd96 (P1) and 0x10fd9c (P2) into the per-port state at 0x10ef22/0x10ef28, computes the newly pressed edges (prev EOR cur AND cur) and holds each edge alive for the auto-repeat delay 0x10ef3a then the period 0x10ef3b; the demo mode instead plays a delta stream (0x852a2) and records it; calls 0x852a2 demo_input_record

Dormant demo recorder: ROM flag $85138 = 0 gates its sole call at $85150. Samples real ports into synthetic input bytes $10ef2e/$10ef2f and records timed XOR-bit toggles in the stream selected by pointer $10ef30; packs changed bits via demo_buf_pack $853b0, appends elapsed counts via demo_buf_put_nibble $85386; cursor reaching $200 clears synthetic inputs and selects stopped source 2.

Demo player: reads the next delta from the record buffer (0x853de) and toggles the matching bit of the synthetic input bytes 0x10ef2e/0x10ef2f (low nibble of the delta = bit index, bit 3 selects P1/P2); calls 0x853de demo_event_next
Appends the pending nibble 0x10ef38 to the record buffer at the write cursor 0x10ef36 and clears the pending nibble

Packs one timed XOR-bit toggle: calls demo_buf_put_nibble $85386, merges d1 bit index into the high nibble of the byte at the old event cursor $10ef34, retaining its delay low nibble, then moves that cursor to write cursor $10ef36; does not play back input.

reads the next demo playback step (W 0x10ef36, P 0x10ef34, T 0x10ef38): d0.b is the input bit index, not a delta; after a saturated delay a nonzero next byte means more delay and a zero byte fires; the stream[512] read happens only after >111,000 calls (modelled over the five 0x84fc8 streams) (semantic-review-p1-844f8)
Arms the memory-card screen: clears the fix layer map (0xf3f2, 0xd0f6), pushes the clear stream 0x862d0 and resumes the screen body at 0x854a8; calls 0xf3f2 fix_clear

Memory-card screen body: checks the card (0x840d8), runs the two entry branches on the result byte 0x10eeb8, draws the summary (0x83dea / 0x856a6 / 0x85812 / 0x858ec) and its save entry runs the save (0x843ae) only with a card detected (0x83dd2 card_detect) and game_mode 0, else exits; carries the score fields at 0x10ef3e; calls 0x840d8 card_data_check_and_reset
Confirmation prompt for the card screen: copies the current result fields into the prompt actor (0x85726), or redraws the summary and waits 0x12c frames before finishing; calls 0x4c6 actor_spawn
Waits the prompt timer, then signals the parent (0x11 = -1) and despawns; calls 0x598
START handler of the card screen: only in a 1P/2P game (0x102eba == 0) does it build the card record (0x858ec) and run the save (0x843ae); calls 0x858ec card_record_build
Draws the five result-field labels/values of the card screen through the fix stream 0xd8c8 and the four number printers; calls 0xd8c8 vram_word_stream
Copies the prompt actor's result fields into the live result block 0x10ef3e

blinks the four statistics fields (not a prompt): nothing happens until +$40 (100) first reaches 0, then bit 5 of the running counter selects draw / fill with tile $ff; 1 draw frame, then 32 erase and 32 draw twice, then 32 erase and a final draw ends the actor; no residue (semantic-review-p1-844f8)

big-font card summary: course name 0x863b0[0x10eeb7] (USA/GERMANY/JAPAN/AUSTRALIA) at x=8 y=5, 'HOLE NO.' and hole_number, golfer type 0x8640a[0x10eeb9] (YOUNG HERO .. TECHNICIAN) at y=11, score 0x10eed6 (EVEN, or '+'/'-' and the magnitude) at y=14 (semantic-review-p1-844f8)

Builds the $80-byte card record at $10eea2: +$14=$ff, +$15=course, +$16=hole (0 for hole 0 or >=$13). The title is written by card_write $8444a. Saved-round branch copies golfer/scores, contest_hole_list and statistics and merges 32 leaderboard rows through $85a24; terminal branch writes $0000ffff score longs, statistics and clears +$40..+$7f, leaving some unused fields untouched (semantic-settle-card-demo).

Merges 32 leaderboard rows (d5=$1f) into the card record: matches each computer name pointer against the course list $83352[course] and stores scores/holes at +$40/+$60; stores the human score/holes at +$34/+$35.

Restores a saved card round: returns for player mask 3 or card hole +$16=0; otherwise restores hole/course and contest_hole_list, golfer and scores into the player record selected by $864ae[mask-1], rebuilds/sorts the leaderboard and assigns competition ranks across 32 rows. Sole caller card_screen_main guarantees mask 1 or 2 on load; external card fields are not validated (semantic-settle-card-demo).

prints 'III.HH / RRR': the cumulative round score 0x10ef3e divided by the completed-round count 0x10ef42 (integer, '.', hundredths, '/', rounds); only the round count is clamped to 0x3e7; game-built records keep total/count <= $ff00 so the divu cannot overflow; calls 0x85e04 bcd_number_draw; no prize amount (semantic-review-p1-844f8)
Prints the round score byte 0x10ef46 at VRAM 0x7372 with the sign glyph (0xbc2 minus, 0xbc0 plus) at 0x73b2; 0x7f prints the empty marker; calls 0x85e04 bcd_number_draw
Prints the holes-played byte 0x10ef44 (clamped to 0x63) at VRAM 0x7376; calls 0x85e04 bcd_number_draw
Prints the rank byte 0x10ef47 (< 0x20) at VRAM 0x737a, or the blank marker 0x862fe when it is zero; calls 0x85e04 bcd_number_draw

Decimal printer: converts d0 through bcd_convert (0x56826) and writes the digits (max d2 digits, sign handling for negative values) into the fix layer at a1 through 0xd7a6, using the digit tile tables 0x862ea; calls 0x56826 bcd_convert

Adds this hole's prize to the result: player byte 0 (0x107076) scaled by 0x100 is added to the prize long 0x10ef3e, the hole counter 0x10ef42 is incremented, and the best score 0x10ef46 / best rank 0x10ef47 are kept from 0x85ffa and 0x85fce; calls 0x73b28
Copies the result fields (0x2a..0x33) and the card byte 0x14 of the record at 0x10eea2 into the live result block 0x10ef3e..0x10ef48
Same copy as 0x85f5e but clears the 0x10ef48 card byte first (no card present)

Returns the player's position (0x83d58) if the player is first and strictly better than the previous second place, else 0 - the "new record" test for the rank field; calls 0x83d58 leaderboard_player_position
Returns the score byte of the leaderboard entry flagged as human (flag bit 3), or 0 when there is none

returns the merged press-edge byte 0x10d52b (move.b $10d52b,d0; rts) in the BIOS pad layout: bit 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right, 4-7 A-D; nothing start-specific; callers 0x83ed4, 0x842da (btst #4) and 0x860a4 (semantic-review-p1-844f8)

AES difficulty select (spawned at $e6d2 in root_attract_title_flow only when BIOS_MVS_FLAG 0x10fd82 == 0): resets the fix layer (0xf3f2) and the sprite allocator (0xd0f6), clears the palette fade flags (0xb99fa), sets the temporary palette stream 0x862dc, spawns the LEVEL SELECT heading 0x578ce and marker_actor 0xf460, installs 0x86070 (semantic-review-p1-844f8)

difficulty select actor: script 0x864b6 (cursor sprite), +$44 = 1 (NORMAL); up/down edges (bits 0/1) step +$44 mod 4 with sound $1067; the A edge plays $1061 and installs 0x86166; draws via 0x8619e; after the fade it writes difficulty_level 0x102eb8 = 0x863ac[+$44] (EASY 0, NORMAL 3, HARD 7, MVS 4); no course factor (semantic-review-p1-844f8)

frame routine after the confirm: blanks the prompt line at $715a (spaces 0x86386), adds 1 to +$43 so the cursor flickers, counts +$40 down from 60 while +$42 == 0, then spawns the fade 0xf42c, sets +$42 = $ff and continues at 0x86110 (semantic-review-p1-844f8)

draws the difficulty words EASY/NORMAL/HARD/MVS in the big font (0xd8c8) at fix x=14 y=10/14/18/22 (0x71ca/0x71ce/0x71d2/0x71d6; streams 0x86320/0x8632a/0x86340/0x86338), the selected one with attribute $5000; then the 'PUSH A BUTTON START' prompt at $715a (0x86372 / spaces 0x86386) blinking on +$43 bit 7; no option boxes or cursor glyph (semantic-review-p1-844f8)
Spawns the fade-in actor 0xb9740 with the per-step delay from d0; calls 0x4c6 actor_spawn
Spawns the fade-out actor 0xb97d2 with the per-step delay from d0; calls 0x4c6 actor_spawn
Spawns the fade-to-colour actor 0xb9890 with the fade parameters; calls 0x4c6 actor_spawn
Second trampoline to the fade-to-colour actor 0xb9890 (variant entry with the same d0..d3 parameters); calls 0x4c6 actor_spawn

Fade-in actor: marks the palette shadow dirty (0x104fc8 = 1), clears the three fade levels and raises them by 3 every 0x40 vblanks until 0x1f, then sets the fade-done byte 0x104fcf and despawns; calls 0x54a actor_despawn
Fade-out actor: sets the fade level bytes to 0x1f and hands over to the stepping body 0xb9814
Fade-out body: lowers the three fade levels by 3 every ($40,a6) vblanks until 0x1f steps are done, then clears the levels, sets 0x104fcf and despawns; calls 0x54a actor_despawn
Spawns the fade-to-colour actor 0xb9890 and stores its four parameters in the actor (+0x4c R, +0x4e G, +0x50 B, +0x40 duration); calls 0x4c6 actor_spawn

Fade-to-colour actor: computes the per-frame deltas for R/G/B from the current levels toward the targets (0x104fca/b/c, 8.8 fixed point, divided by the duration) and steps them every frame, writing the levels back; at the end it snaps to the targets, sets 0x104fcf and despawns; calls 0x54a actor_despawn

Clears the whole palette-slot table: every record at 0x102fc8 is set to $8800/zero, the free list 0x102ec2, its cursors 0x102fc4/0x102fc6 and the counter 0x102fc2 are reset, and the fade flags are cleared
Clears the palette dirty/fade flags 0x104fc8, 0x104fca/b/c, 0x104fcf and 0x104fd0; called at screen transitions
Returns d2 = -1 and ($20,a6) = the slot when the actor already holds the palette d1 (searches the actor's list at +0x22 with count +0x2a backwards); otherwise d2 = 0

Force-allocates a palette slot for the actor without the dedup check (same ring/free-list mechanics as 0xb9a22, record flags 0x04|0x01); only caller pose_panel_actor at $7b91a. Static live-actor/palette accounting gives free >=15 at every call, so the zero-free exit to $b9b00 with saved registers still on stack is unreachable (semantic-settle-r2-palslot).

Word stream command handler: for each 4-byte record {u16 slot id 0x10..0x40 or 0xff, u16 palette id or -1} it points the slot record's source at 0xad730 + id*0x40 with refcount 1 (0xff releases the slot, -1 marks it released), until the -1 terminator

Tail of the palette stream handler 0xb9bde: reads the next stream word, terminates on -1 and otherwise masks the slot id; reached by the back-branches of the adjacent block and guarded by the trap at 0xb9c48
Closing loop of the palette stream handler (slot releases and the trap guard); the record layout and terminator are the same as 0xb9bde
Variant of the palette stream handler using the temporary palette bank 0xb7ef0 instead of 0xad730 (slots 0x00..0x40, 0xff = release), for palettes built at runtime

Releases one reference of hardware slot d1: decrements the record refcount, and at zero marks the slot free (0x80 flag plus 0x08), clears its source, and pushes the slot id back onto the free ring 0x102ec2 (cursor 0x102fc6, count 0x102fc2)
Sets a slot's source to the temporary palette bank 0xb7ef0 (entry point of the 0xb9d90 body)
Points slot d1 at palette d2 of the bank (0xad730), sets the animation period d3 (from/target delay) and the byte +0x0f from d4, and marks the record 0x02 (animated)
Sets the "skip upload" bit 3 on slot d1 (the palette is animated in place, so the vblank upload must leave it alone)
Clears the "skip upload" bit 3 on slot d1

Per-vblank palette driver: installs the palette-wipe task 0xca926 when the wipe counter 0x104fd1 is not 0xff; then, unless the animation path owns the frame, applies the pending fade/cross-fade to every slot record (0xca4e6 for animated slots, 0xca4b0 for dirty ones, 0xca6fc/0xca766 for fade-mode slots) and copies the RGB through the RGB555 table 0xba030 into the shadow at 0x104fd2 + slot*0x20, clearing the dirty bit and setting the shadow's first word so palette_upload picks the slot up; calls 0xca4b0 palette_upload_slot_copy
Copies one palette (16 colours, a2 = source in (R,G,B,0) 5-bit form) into the shadow slot a3 through the RGB555 table 0xba030 and clears the slot's dirty bit, setting the shadow dirty word 1
Releases every hardware slot the actor holds (walks its palette list at +0x22 backwards through 0xb9d20 and clears the entries); calls 0xb9d20 palette_slot_free
Expands a Neo Geo colour word in d4 into the packed 15-bit RGB555 form (bits 14-10 R, 9-5 G, 4-0 B) by shifting the colour word's planes; the dark bit is dropped
Packs the RGB555 value in d4 into a Neo Geo colour word (dark bit 0, R0/G0/B0 in bits 14/13/12); inverse of 0xca7d6
Clears the whole palette shadow: writes 0x100 longs of 0 to 0x104fd2 (the loop body is the adjacent block at 0xca874, whose dbra targets 0xca872); called by `jsr $ca866.l` at 0xd682
Clear-loop body (8 longs plus dbra back to 0xca872, clr.b 0x104fd1) that closes the palette-shadow reset, then tail-jumps to 0xb99a8
Entry of the palette wipe task: selects the second palette bank latch (0x3a001f = 1) and points a0 at palette RAM 0x400000; the covered block at 0xca934 continues with the 512-byte block wipe

Palette-RAM wipe task (installed by the driver 0xb9de6 through 0xd510): zeroes a 512-byte block of palette RAM at 0x400000 + counter*0x200, writes the palette bank latch 0x3a000f, and advances/wraps the counter 0x104fd1
Wipe-done predicate: returns with carry set when the wipe counter 0x104fd1 has reached 0xff (all blocks cleared)
